sections.heading: C — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
sections.markdown:
## C — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
An arrest for DWUI followed by a chemical-test alcohol concentration of at least 0.08 percent triggers an Administrative Per Se suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Dismissing the court DWUI case does not undo the Administrative Per Se suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
The Administrative Per Se suspension lasts 90 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
If a DWUI conviction follows, time served on the Administrative Per Se suspension is credited toward the DWUI suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
An Administrative Per Se suspension begins 30 days after the officer issues the temporary license and suspension notice, or after an existing suspension or revocation ends. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
The officer's form explains how to seek limited privileges or a contested-case hearing after the administrative action. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
Limited privileges after Administrative Per Se action may be available only to an otherwise eligible driver without a probationary license issued in the previous five years or an ignition-interlock requirement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Administrative Per Se reinstatement requires completing every suspension action on record and paying the reinstatement fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
The DWUI suspension category described here follows a court conviction for driving under the influence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
A DWUI case may also result in deferred prosecution under W.S. 7-13-301. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
A first DWUI offense within the previous 10 years carries a 90-day suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
For that first DWUI, an Administrative Per Se suspension already served or being served uses the same suspension period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
Limited privileges for a first DWUI may be available to an otherwise eligible driver without a probationary license in the past five years or an interlock requirement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
For a first DWUI with arrest BAC at least 0.15 percent, the driver must hold an interlock-restricted license for six months before another license type is available. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
The first-DWUI reinstatement checklist allows completion of suspension actions or, when arrest BAC is at least 0.15 percent, an interlock-restricted application supported by installation proof. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
The first-DWUI reinstatement checklist also requires an SR-22 filing and payment of the reinstatement fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
A second DWUI within the previous 10 years carries a one-year suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
For that second DWUI, an Administrative Per Se suspension already served or underway is followed by an additional nine-month suspension on the record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
A second alcohol-involved DWUI conviction requires an interlock-restricted license for one year before eligibility for another license type. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A03
A third or later DWUI offense within 10 years carries a three-year revocation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A03
A fourth or later alcohol-involved DWUI conviction brings a lifetime interlock-restricted-license requirement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A03
A driver with that lifetime interlock requirement may petition the court for removal five years after the conviction date. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
The third-or-later DWUI reinstatement checklist includes completing suspension or revocation actions or, when required, applying for an interlock-restricted license with installation proof. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
The third-or-later DWUI reinstatement checklist requires filing an SR-22 and paying the reinstatement fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

sections.heading: C — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
sections.markdown:
## C — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
Reinstatement after a third or later DWUI requires an alcohol or drug evaluation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
Reinstatement after a third or later DWUI requires successful completion of an alcohol or drug treatment program. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
The third-or-later DWUI reinstatement checklist calls for passing a re-examination of safe vehicle operation, subject to the stated interlock-license waiver. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
A driver relicensed after the repeat-DWUI process may receive a no-alcohol-or-substance-abuse-offenses restriction and must follow the counselor's recommendations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A03
When an interlock-restricted license has been obtained without violations, the repeat-DWUI re-examination and additional restriction may be waived. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A04
A driver under 21 who has actual physical control of a vehicle with alcohol concentration at least 0.02 percent is subject to the youthful-driver DWUI suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A04
The first youthful-driver DWUI offense carries a 90-day suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A04
A second or later youthful-driver DWUI offense within two years carries a six-month suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A04
Limited privileges in the youthful-driver category may be available to an otherwise eligible applicant with no probationary license in the previous five years and no interlock requirement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A04
For the first youthful-driver offense with arrest BAC at least 0.15 percent, an interlock-restricted license must be held for six months before another license type. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A04
A second youthful-driver DWUI conviction involving alcohol requires one year holding an interlock-restricted license before another license type becomes available. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A04
A reckless-driving suspension follows a conviction for operating a vehicle with willful or wanton disregard for people or property safety. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A04
A first reckless-driving offense within the previous five years carries a 90-day suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A04
Limited privileges after that first reckless-driving offense may be available if the person is otherwise eligible and has had no probationary license in the past five years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A05
A second reckless-driving offense within the previous five years carries a six-month suspension. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F40 | anchor: A05
Limited privileges after a second reckless-driving offense may be available to an otherwise eligible person without a probationary license in the past five years. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F41 | anchor: A05
Second-offense reckless-driving reinstatement requires completing all suspension actions, filing an SR-22 and paying the reinstatement fee. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F42 | anchor: A05
A third or later reckless-driving offense within five years causes a one-year revocation. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F43 | anchor: A05
The third-or-later reckless-driving category does not allow limited driving privileges. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F44 | anchor: A05
Third-or-later reckless-driving reinstatement requires completion of recorded suspension or revocation actions, an SR-22, the reinstatement fee and a passed safe-driving re-examination. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F45 | anchor: A05
A conviction involving intent to furnish alcoholic liquor or malt beverage to someone under 21 while operating or occupying a motor vehicle triggers the transporting-liquor-to-a-minor suspension. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F46 | anchor: A05
The transporting-liquor-to-a-minor suspension lasts one year. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F47 | anchor: A05
Limited privileges after the transporting-liquor conviction may be available to an otherwise eligible person who has had no probationary license in the last five years. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F48 | anchor: A05
Reinstatement after the transporting-liquor suspension requires completion of all suspension actions and payment of the reinstatement fee. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0023]

Misconceptions: Court dismissal does not necessarily remove an administrative suspension, and a petition to remove a lifetime requirement is not automatic removal.
Mnemonics: Recall index: trigger, lookback, action, exception, reinstatement; this organizer adds no penalty or legal interpretation.
Glossary: Recall terms: administrative suspension, DWUI, revocation, probationary license, interlock-restricted license and financial-responsibility certificate.
Dynamic facts: Fee amounts, installer lists and phone numbers are withheld as updatable debt. All penalty rules remain tied to the staged edition and require current applicability review.

items.skill: Distinguish administrative and court DWUI actions
items.why: The source gives separate triggers and credit rules.
Different suspension categories use different age and time conditions.

items.skill: Distinguish insurance proofs and reinstatement steps
items.why: Crash-related alternatives differ from compulsory-insurance conviction procedures.

items.skill: Identify review deadlines and interlock eligibility
items.why: Notice dates and documentary prerequisites matter.
